en: The Apadāna of the Elder Atthasandassaka Sobhita Chapter 7 I was a teacher of the Vedas, well-versed in the three Vedas. I was a reciter of the hymns, possessing great fame and renown. I was a master of the six Vedāṅgas and a knower of the five sciences. I was a teacher of the Vedas, skilled in the exposition of the meaning. At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, the Teacher of the World, appeared in the world. He was the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, and Bhagavān. Having heard of the appearance of the Buddha in the world, I went to him with a retinue of five hundred. Having approached the Blessed One, I paid homage at his feet and sat down to one side. As I sat there, the Blessed One taught me the Dhamma, which is excellent in the beginning, excellent in the middle, and excellent in the end, both in meaning and in phrasing; he revealed the holy life, which is perfectly complete and pure. Having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. Then, having taken refuge in the Triple Gem, I took up the five precepts. Having established myself in the five precepts, I became a lay follower. Then, having passed away from that state, I was reborn in the realm of the Thirty-three gods. There, for many hundreds of thousands of years, I enjoyed celestial pleasures. Having passed away from the realm of the Thirty-three, I was reborn in the human world. In this final existence, I was born into a noble family in Sāvatthī. When I had grown up, I went forth into homelessness under the Blessed One. Having gone forth, I applied myself to meditation and attained the fruit of arhatship. I am now an arhat, free from all taints, one who has done what was to be done, laid down the burden, achieved his own goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, and is liberated through perfect knowledge. This is my Apadāna. May it be auspicious.
Seated in the spacious hall,
I beheld the Leader of the World,
whose taints were exhausted and who had attained the powers.
Honored by the community of monks—
those possessing the threefold knowledge, endowed with the six superknowledges, and great in psychic power, numbering one hundred thousand.
They attend upon the Fully Awakened One;
who, having seen him, would not find confidence?
For whom could there even be a comparison with his wisdom?
In this world with its devas,
who that has seen the Perfectly Awakened One of infinite wisdom would not find confidence?
They are unable to conceive of him who reveals the Dhammakāya, that sole treasury of jewels.
Who, having seen this, would not have faith?
By these three verses,
Nārada, who is compassionate toward those called by his name;
Having praised the Sambuddha Padumuttara, the unconquered,
through that clarity of mind,
And by means of praising the Buddhas,
for a hundred thousand eons,
I did not fall into an evil rebirth.
In the three hundredth aeon from now,
there will be a kṣatriya named Sumitta,
endowed with the seven treasures.
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Such is the teaching of the Buddha.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Atthasandassaka speak these verses.
This is the seventh legend of the elder Atthasandassaka.
